threats.title: JWT Token Replay Attack
threats.description: JWT tokens issued by /api/auth/login lack expiry enforcement in the transfer endpoint middleware. Tokens captured via network interception or XSS remain valid indefinitely.
attack_path: Attacker captures JWT via XSS or MITM

threats.title: Blockchain Double-Spend via Race Condition
threats.description: The token transfer function reads balance, then writes new balance in two separate DB operations without atomic locking. Concurrent requests can read the same pre-deducted balance.
attack_path: Fires N transfer requests concurrently with same nonce
Race condition allows multiple transfers from single balance
prerequisites: Ability to send concurrent HTTP requests
detection_indicators: Multiple transfers in <100ms from same account
Duplicate nonce values in transaction log

threats.title: IDOR on Order Endpoints
threats.description: Order IDs are sequential integers. The GET /api/orders/{id} endpoint validates authentication but not ownership — any authenticated user can enumerate and read any order.
attack_path: Access PII, payment methods, and order history of all users
detection_indicators: User accessing orders with non-matching user_id
High volume of 200 OK responses on order endpoints

threats.title: SSRF via Webhook URL
threats.description: The webhook configuration endpoint accepts arbitrary URLs for callback notifications. The server fetches the URL to validate connectivity, enabling SSRF to internal services, cloud metadata APIs, and private network ranges.
attack_path: Server fetches URL, returns AWS metadata including IAM credentials
detection_indicators: Requests to RFC1918 ranges from app server

threats.title: Privilege Escalation via Role Parameter Manipulation
threats.description: The profile update endpoint accepts a 'role' field in the request body. Server-side validation is missing — users can upgrade their own role to 'admin' or 'compliance_officer'.
attack_path: Re-authenticate — now has full admin privileges
detection_indicators: role field present in PATCH body
User role change without admin-initiated action

threats.title: Smart Contract Reentrancy
threats.description: The token withdrawal smart contract calls the external recipient contract before updating the internal balance. An attacker's malicious contract can recursively call withdraw() before the balance is zeroed, draining the pool.
attack_path: Deploy malicious contract with receive() that re-calls withdraw()
Call withdraw() on token pool contract
Recursion drains entire pool before state update
detection_indicators: Pool balance dropping to zero in single transaction
Gas usage anomaly on withdrawal txn

threats.title: Mass Account Takeover via Credential Stuffing
threats.description: Login endpoint has no effective rate limiting per IP or account. No CAPTCHA, no bot detection, no credential stuffing protection. Allows automated testing of leaked credential databases.
attack_path: Successful logins grant full account access

threats.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
threats.description: PATCHED: The search endpoint previously concatenated user input directly into SQL query. Now uses parameterized queries. Verified via regression test suite.
threats.fix_applied: Migrated to parameterized queries via ORM (SQLAlchemy). Regression tests: test_search_sql_injection_blocked().

threats.title: Delivery Address Tampering via IDOR
threats.description: Delivery address IDs are exposed in the update endpoint without ownership verification. A user may be able to modify delivery addresses belonging to other users.

threats.title: API Credentials Hardcoded in Mobile APK
threats.description: Static analysis of the decompiled Android APK reveals hardcoded API keys and internal service URLs in the res/values/strings.xml and BuildConfig.java files.
attack_path: Use keys to access internal APIs directly
detection_indicators: API key patterns in decompiled source

threats.title: Unrestricted File Upload leading to RCE
threats.description: Product image upload endpoint validates file extension client-side only. Accepts .php, .jsp, and other executable files if content-type header is spoofed. Uploaded files are served from web-accessible directory.
attack_path: Upload PHP webshell with content-type: image/jpeg
Execute arbitrary OS commands as web server user
detection_indicators: Non-image MIME types in upload endpoint
Script file extensions in upload directory
Unusual processes spawned by web server

threats.title: Token Supply Inflation via Mint Race Condition
threats.description: The token minting function checks total supply, computes new mint amount, then updates supply in non-atomic steps. A race condition allows the supply check to pass multiple times before any update is committed, inflating total supply beyond cap.
attack_path: All pass total_supply < MAX_SUPPLY check simultaneously
All mint operations execute — supply exceeds cap
threats.owasp_category: Smart Contract Top 10: SC04 Integer Overflow / Underflow
detection_indicators: Multiple mint events in same block
